title: A false bounded loop yields an index at which the predicate fails
statement: If the bounded loop allBelow f n evaluates to false then there is an index i below n at which f i is false.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Finset.allBelow_false_witness : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.allBelow x0 x1) Bool.false) -> Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x3 : AxNat) => And (AxNat.lt x3 x1) (Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x3) Bool.false)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.Finset.allBelow_false_witness is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(target/release/examples/kernel_declaration_projection 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cF '-> Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x3 : AxNat) => And (AxNat.lt x3 x1) (Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x3) Bool.false)))))')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is a DISTINGUISHING substring of the admitted type, not the declaration's name: an existence check would still pass if the statement drifted. Verified to hit ZERO on a perturbed pattern before this row was written -- see the mutation table in ADR-1593. `kernel_declaration_projection` prints every declaration with its footprint size and its rendered type, and the prelude build admits this theorem only through the trusted gate, so a successful build IS the type-check.

evidence.supports: The statement says what its name says -- checked at a concrete instance with hand-computed numerals and paired with the specific wrong statement it rules out
evidence.notes: The trusted gate cannot tell a THEOREM's statement is not what its name says: a `card_le_of_injOn` with its two `card`s transposed, an `exists_collision` whose pair need not be DISTINCT, or a `pigeonhole` whose strict inequality points the other way would each be admitted, carry an empty axiom footprint, and pass every other row in this ledger. `nat_prelude/finset_pigeonhole_tests.rs` instantiates each statement at a concrete pair of sets whose cardinalities are computed independently, and pairs every positive with the wrong statement it rules out. Three of its controls are the sharper kind, where a hypothesis cannot be DISCHARGED (`infer` must fail) rather than a conclusion merely being false.

notes: allBelow's third law, and the SEARCH direction. F:nat-finset-all-below-of-all-true builds the loop and F:nat-finset-all-below-true-at reads a true one back pointwise; neither says anything about a false one, which is exactly what a refuted decision hands you. The recursion IS the search, so the witness is COMPUTED rather than chosen and no choice principle appears -- at f j = false the top index is the answer, at f j = true the guard reduces to the shorter loop and the induction hypothesis's index is re-introduced at the widened bound. ADR-1593.
